question.problem:
The Cartesian equation of the ellipse defined by the parametric equations

$$
x=5\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -4,\,y=3\sqrt{3}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +2,\,0\le \theta <2\pi .
$$

is given by

{{field-1}}
$=1.$
question.worked_solution:
To find the Cartesian equation of the ellipse, we need to eliminate the parameter $\theta .$ We can do this using the Pythagorean theorem.

By isolating the $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ term in the $x$-equation and squaring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =5\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -4 \\ \frac{x+4}{5} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{(x+4)^{2}}{{5}^{2}} & ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{(x+4)^{2}}{25} & ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

By isolating the $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ term in the $y$-equation and squaring, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =3\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +2 \\ \frac{y-2}{3\sqrt{3}} & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{(y-2)^{2}}{(3\sqrt{3})^{2}} & ={sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{(y-2)^{2}}{27} & ={sin}^{2}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the two equations and using ${cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta =1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x+4)^{2}}{25}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{27} & ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta =1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the Cartesian equation of the ellipse is

$$
\frac{(x+4)^{2}}{25}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{27}=1.
$$
